principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum); DESIGN_LANGUAGE §2 (pure-black base, never grey/white)
location: src/app/not-found.tsx (missing) — Next.js default not-found boundary
problem: Any unknown route (e.g. /tools/color-wheel, /signin) renders Next.js's UNTHEMED default 404: body background is forced to white rgb(255,255,255) with near-white text rgb(245,245,245) — measured contrast ~1.04:1 (text invisible) and a full-screen white flash inside a pure-black terminal app. Breaks the aesthetic and fails AA catastrophically.
fix: Add a themed src/app/not-found.tsx (and global-error.tsx) rendered inside the terminal shell: #0A0A0A bg, cyan '404' + phosphor body, a 'RETURN TO DASHBOARD' link. Do NOT let the Next default boundary leak its white background.

principle: DESIGN_LANGUAGE §4 (Primary=cyan, Secondary=yellow/green, Tertiary=green-outline); Refactoring UI Hierarchy; Laws of UX — Von Restorff & Fitts
location: recipes list (ASSIGN green / SHARE yellow / NEW RECIPE green-outline); recipe detail (SAVE green / ASSIGN cyan / SHARE cyan-outline / DELETE red); dashboard (IMPORT yellow / NEW PROJECT green / ADD green); sign-in (SIGN IN dim grey-cyan)
problem: Button tiers are inconsistent page-to-page and the cyan Primary is rarely the actual primary action. The page's most important CTA is often a quiet outline (NEW RECIPE) while row-level secondary actions shout in solid yellow/green; three solid colors compete side-by-side (dashboard IMPORT yellow + NEW PROJECT green + ADD green); ASSIGN is green on the list page but cyan on the detail page; sign-in's primary CTA is a desaturated grey-cyan, not brand cyan.
fix: Codify ONE button system as components: btn-primary = solid cyan #00D2FF + black text (exactly one per view, the dominant action); btn-secondary = green/yellow solid; btn-tertiary = ghost/outline. Audit every page — make the single dominant CTA cyan-solid, demote the rest. Sign-in 'SIGN IN' → cyan-solid. One color for 'assign' everywhere.

area: Panels — grey fills (Planner, Project detail, Sign-in card, Match)
principle: DESIGN_LANGUAGE §2 & §5 ('Kill ALL grey fills → transparent/black panels — never grey'); REDESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF §2 (Ross's named BAD example: 'grey background on dashboard elements — just make it transparent')
location: /planner FOCUS & INSPO panels; /projects/[id] OPS·RECIPE / OPS·ROSTER panels; /sign-in card; /tools/match left filter block
problem: Several panels render with a visible grey / grey-gradient fill instead of black/transparent. The Dashboard panels are correctly black, so the app contradicts itself page-to-page. This is the exact failure Ross called out by name as why the old app 'lost the aesthetic'; it makes Planner and Project detail read as generic dark-SaaS rather than terminal-OS.
fix: Replace panel background tokens on these surfaces with the black/transparent panel token used on the Dashboard (transparent or #0A0A0A) + 1px phosphor nested border + corner ticks. Make a single <Panel> component the only way panels are built so this can't drift again.

principle: UX-UI-BEST-PRACTICES §9 (monospace body min 15px; mono reads ~15% smaller); WCAG 2.2 §1.4.4
location: Body/table/label text app-wide — measured 135 nodes @11px + 110 @13px on /projects; 53 @11px + 243 @13px on /library
problem: The app leans heavily on 11px and 13px IBM Plex Mono for table cells, labels, filter rails and tags. Monospace at 11px is below the legibility floor for this aesthetic and reads noticeably smaller than 11px sans. On the dense table/library surfaces this hurts the 'readable' hard floor the brief insists on.
fix: Raise the mono floor: table cells/body 13px → 14px, micro-labels/tech-ticks 11px → 12px min, base body ~15px. Use rem so browser zoom works. Keep the type scale on the constrained set (12/14/16/18/...).

principle: NN/g Heuristic 1 (Visibility of system status); Jakob's Law (recognition of location)
location: Left nav rail + mobile bottom tab bar on /projects/[id]
problem: On a project-detail page the nav highlights DASHBOARD as active (cyan + ▸ marker) on both desktop and mobile, giving no correct location cue. Library/Wishlist/Tools set active state correctly, so this is project-detail-specific.
fix: Either keep DASHBOARD active intentionally (it is the projects section) AND add a clearer in-page 'you are here' cue, or add a distinct PROJECTS active state. Make it consistent with the breadcrumb (SYS ▸ UNIT / WORKSPACE).

principle: REDESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF §1 group 27 (FAVORITE: cyan-highlighted selected row, quick-action buttons, 5-color palette); Refactoring UI Hierarchy; NN/g Heuristic 5
location: /projects DB·PROJECTS table
problem: The mission table is the surface the moodboard FAVORITE (group 27) maps to, but it reads as a flat, evenly-weighted row list. There is no cyan-highlighted selected/active row (the single most-cited group-27 love), rows have near-equal visual weight so the 5-second scan finds no priority, and a destructive DELETE link sits exposed on every row. The TYPE/RECIPE/STATUS color-bar tags ARE good and on-brand.
fix: (1) Add a cyan-highlighted 'active/focused' row (cyan left-border + faint cyan tint) keyed to the Focus project. (2) Establish row hierarchy: brighten active/priority rows, dim shelved/complete. (3) Replace always-visible row DELETE with a hover/▸ menu + confirm. (4) Right-align + tabular-nums the completion column and use the SegmentedBar viz instead of the thin inline bar.

principle: DESIGN_LANGUAGE §6 (Ross chose MEDIUM: 'medium scanlines + restrained phosphor glow'); UX-UI-BEST-PRACTICES §9
location: Global background / screen overlay — no fixed scanline layer detected in computed styles
problem: Computed-style inspection found NO scanline overlay and no CRT texture; only a subtle h1 cyan text-shadow glow renders. Ross explicitly chose 'Medium' CRT. The app reads cleaner/flatter than the chosen setting — closer to dark-SaaS than terminal-OS. The terminal 'character' the rebuild is meant to re-inject is most missing on the calmer pages (Recipes, Planner, Tools landing).
fix: Add the spec's static repeating-linear-gradient scanline overlay (fixed, pointer-events:none, ~12% alpha) on the app shell, guarded by prefers-reduced-motion; optionally a one-time boot/flicker flourish. Re-check contrast after. Cheapest single move to make every page read 'terminal'.

area: Dashboard KPI cards — mobile label truncation & overlap
principle: Refactoring UI (design for real content); WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow
location: /projects KPI grid at 390px (LEAD·01..STAT·04)
problem: At 390px the 2-up KPI cards truncate headings ('ACTIVE PROJ…', 'AVG COMPLET…', 'PAINTING TI…') and the AVG COMPLETION radial gauge overlaps its 'ACROSS PROJECTS' caption inside the card. Labels were sized for desktop width.
fix: On mobile let KPI labels wrap to 2 lines (no ellipsis) or shorten them (ACTIVE / AVG DONE / STREAK / TIME); give the radial gauge its own row above the caption in the card grid so they can't collide.

principle: NN/g Heuristic 2 + Heuristic 8; REDESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF §1 group 21 ('memory element / color-map')
location: /library right panel 'MEM · COVERAGE'
problem: The colorful pixel/memory grid is a strong custom-graphic moment and clearly the group-21 'memory/color-map' reference — but it has no legend or labels explaining what a cell means (brands owned? hue coverage? paint count?). It currently reads as decoration, risking the moodboard's 'boring/meaningless data-viz' BAD bucket despite looking good.
fix: Add a one-line legend + bucket labels (e.g. 'each cell = one hue bucket; brightness = paints owned') and make cells hover/tap to filter the catalog. Tie it to real coverage data so it earns its space.

area: Recipes list & Tools landing — unframed / empty
principle: Refactoring UI (empty != minimal); REDESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF §1 ('row of folders that open a window'); DESIGN_LANGUAGE §5 (nested panels)
location: /recipes (bare table on empty field); /tools (4 text rows, no tiles)
problem: Recipes and the Tools landing are the most 're-skinned, not designed' surfaces. Recipes is a plain table floating in ~60% empty black with blank thumbnail slots and 'no palette yet' on every row. Tools lists 4 utilities as bare text rows rather than the enclosed file/folder tiles the moodboard favors. Neither uses the nested-border panel language that unifies the rest of the OS.
fix: Wrap Recipes in a nested-border panel with corner ticks + a RECIPES·N header rail; render rows as cards with the swatch thumbnail filled (or a placeholder glyph). Convert Tools into a 2x2 grid of folder/file tiles ('boxes with black/no fill', group 27) that 'open' on hover. Fill the dead lower space with a relevant module rather than void.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, 24px); Apple HIG / Material (44–48px recommended)
location: /projects: 17 interactive elements < 24px (row name links ~17px tall, filter input ~17px, ↗ links); /library: 86 < 24px (row checkboxes, star/icon buttons)
problem: Measured: many interactive controls fall below the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum — mostly 17px-tall table row links, tiny row checkboxes, and icon-only star/clone buttons. On mobile these are mis-tap risks.
fix: Raise interactive min-height to ≥24px (prefer 44px on mobile): pad table row links and the filter input vertically, enlarge icon-button hit areas (44px touch zone even if the glyph stays small), grow row checkboxes. Pairs naturally with the UX-004 type-floor bump.

principle: DESIGN_LANGUAGE §3 (Title face = Digital Arcade/PixelSplitter, sparing, page-top only); Refactoring UI Typography
location: DASHBOARD (stylized title) vs RECIPES / FOCUS / TOOLS / LIBRARY / recipe-detail / project-detail titles (plain mono)
problem: The Dashboard uses a distinct stylized title treatment; most other page titles render in the same mono as body, just larger + cyan. The signature title face that signals 'page top' is applied unevenly, weakening the OS identity and inter-page hierarchy.
fix: Decide once: apply the title face to every page H1 consistently, OR reserve it for the Dashboard hero only and give all other H1s one consistent treatment. Apply everywhere.

area: Destructive actions exposed (Project & Recipe detail, table rows)
principle: NN/g Heuristic 5 (error prevention) & Heuristic 3 (user control); Universal Principles (prevent over handle)
location: /projects/[id] 'DELETE PROJECT' (top-right, above fold); /recipes/[id] 'DELETE RECIPE' (under title); per-row DELETE in dashboard table
problem: Destructive deletes get premium, always-visible placement (top of project detail, under recipe title, every table row). On mobile DELETE PROJECT sits above the fold next to a wrapping title — easy to mis-tap. No visible confirm affordance observed at the button.
fix: Demote destructive actions: move DELETE into an overflow/▸ menu or page bottom, render as red-outline (not solid), require a confirm step. Standardize across project, recipe, and table-row deletes.

area: Focus/Planner missing from mobile nav; stopwatch hidden
principle: Hick's/Miller's Law (nav completeness); NN/g Heuristic 6; DESIGN_LANGUAGE §8 (Focus stopwatch is a signature element)
location: Mobile bottom tab bar (Dashboard/Library/Recipes/Tools/Wishlist — FOCUS absent); /planner empty state
problem: Desktop nav has FOCUS as a top-level item but the mobile bottom tab bar omits it (only 5 of 6 sections reachable). Focus is a core 'sit down and paint' flow. Separately, the Focus page's promised stopwatch/TIMER is invisible in the empty state — the headline says 'run the stopwatch' but there is no stopwatch surface until a recipe is attached, so the signature feature is undiscoverable.
fix: Add FOCUS to the mobile nav (6th tab or a 'more' affordance if 5 is the cap). On /planner, show the stopwatch/TIMER shell even in the empty state (disabled with a hint) so the feature is visible before setup.

area: Custom-graphic coverage — only auth has bespoke art
principle: Laws of UX — Aesthetic-Usability & Peak-End; REDESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF §3 (custom-graphic opportunities, parked isometric hero); DESIGN_LANGUAGE §7.4 & §13
location: Sign-in isometric CRT hero (exists, excellent) vs Dashboard / project detail / empty states (no bespoke art)
problem: The only bespoke illustration in the app is the sign-in isometric CRT-computer hero — and it is the best-looking screen, proving the payoff. Everywhere else relies on the (good) SVG viz kit but has no signature illustration. The parked isometric/wireframe-globe/3D-city hero (group 20/23) has not landed on any in-app surface, so the dashboard's 5-second 'wow' is carried by gauges alone.
fix: Build the parked wireframe-globe or isometric 'workbench/city' hero (DESIGN_LANGUAGE §13) and place ONE instance on the Dashboard (or Focus) as the signature viz. Add small bespoke spot-illustrations to key empty states (empty Focus, empty roster, no-recipes) — empty states are first impressions.

principle: Refactoring UI (don't double-encode); NN/g Heuristic 8 (minimalist)
location: /projects/[id] top: circular '0% DONE' gauge + a linear '0%' progress bar immediately below
problem: The same completion metric is shown twice within ~40px: a small circular gauge top-right and a full-width linear bar under the title. Redundant; the small gauge is also visually disconnected from the title block.
fix: Keep one. Either make the circular gauge the hero stat (larger, group-20 styled, with a per-stage breakdown ring) and drop the linear bar, or keep the linear bar and remove the small gauge. If both stay, make them show different things (overall vs per-stage).

area: Wishlist table horizontal overflow at desktop
principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow; Refactoring UI
location: /wishlist PAINTS·QUEUE table at 1440 — right-edge 'WISHLIST ▾' status control clipped
problem: The PAINTS queue table is wider than the content column at 1440px; the rightmost status dropdown ('WISHLIST ▾') is clipped at the viewport edge.
fix: Constrain the table to content width with horizontal scroll inside a bordered panel, or drop/condense a low-value column (PRICE/VENDOR are empty in real data) so the status control fits. Right-pad the last column.

principle: Refactoring UI (design with real content); REDESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF §6 (5-second read)
location: /recipes ('no palette yet' x6, empty thumbnails); /wishlist (PRICE/VENDOR/CATEGORY all '—')
problem: Across Recipes and Wishlist the value columns are empty (—), thumbnails are blank. While partly a seed-data artifact, the UI does nothing graceful with the sparsity — empty cells read as 'broken/unfinished' rather than 'nothing here yet'.
fix: Design the partial-empty state per column: muted '—' with a tooltip 'add a vendor URL to fill price', a placeholder swatch glyph for recipes with no palette, and consider hiding always-empty columns until populated. (Also reseed demo data with realistic names for future audits.)

area: Background token vs spec (informational — implementation made the better call)
principle: UX-UI-BEST-PRACTICES §9 (use #0D0D0D not #000000 — halation); DESIGN_LANGUAGE §2 (states --color-bg #000000)
location: body background computed = rgb(10,10,10) / #0A0A0A
problem: The implemented base background is #0A0A0A, which is BETTER for halation/OLED than the pure #000000 the DESIGN_LANGUAGE token specifies. Not a defect — flagged only because spec and build disagree, so the token doc should be reconciled to avoid a future 'fix' back to pure black.
fix: Update DESIGN_LANGUAGE §2 --color-bg to #0A0A0A (keep the implemented value) and note the halation rationale. No code change needed.

principle: Refactoring UI (labels vs values, don't repeat); REDESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF §1 ('color bars with black text')
location: /tools/wheel RECIPE COLOURS rows — 'PRIMARY · PRIMARY' duplicate label
problem: Recipe-colour rows show the role label twice ('PRIMARY · PRIMARY'). Minor, but on an otherwise exemplary surface it reads as a placeholder artifact.
fix: Show the role once (slot name + hex tag). The color-bar-with-black-text tag idiom is correct — just drop the duplicate.
